# `•memory` — Memory

`•memory x` gives a record of what this thread holds for differentiation, whatever `x` is. `•memory 0` is the usual spelling.

- `records` counts the record nodes alive: the linear calls that reverse mode records while `∂` runs. Each `∂` frees its record when it returns, so the count is 0 between programs.

The count covers the thread that runs the session. A session on another thread doesn't change it.

```bpl
{+/⍵×⍵}∂ 1 2 3     ⍝ 2 4 6
•memory 0          ⍝ ["records":0ₓ]
```

[`•explain`](explain.qmd) reports what happened while an expression ran.
